task: First find the key and pick it up. Then open the locked door, enter the room, and pick up the ball.

calls.candidate: hard Precedence(has_matching_key, target_door_open), hard Precedence(target_room_entered, target_door_open), hard Precedence(target_room_entered, target_picked_up), soft Existence(target_picked_up)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: several defects. (1) The task unconditionally commands 'pick up the ball', so Existence(target_picked_up) must be hard, not soft; as soft it leaves the task rule-only with an empty FINAL_STATES, so nothing is actually required to happen. Make it hard; with the Precedence(target_room_entered, target_picked_up) chain it also forces target_room_entered, so no Existence for the room is needed. (2) The clause 'open the locked door, enter the room' is compiled as Precedence(target_room_entered, target_door_open): 'target_door_open may not happen before the first target_room_entered', the reverse of the task, which says open the door, then enter. Swap the arguments to Precedence(target_door_open, target_room_entered); together with the hard Existence(target_picked_up) it forces the door to open. (3) Keep Precedence(has_matching_key, target_door_open), which then forces the key to be picked up; no extra Existence clauses are needed.

calls.candidate: hard Existence(target_picked_up), hard Precedence(has_matching_key, target_door_open), hard Precedence(target_door_open, target_room_entered), hard Precedence(target_room_entered, target_picked_up)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: The task states an order between finding the key and picking it up ('First find the key and pick it up'), but no clause records it. The candidate only has Precedence(has_matching_key, target_door_open); nothing requires key_found to precede has_matching_key. Per the environment's Constraints, has_matching_key cannot become true before key_found, but that fact does not make the stated order clause redundant. Add a hard Precedence(key_found, has_matching_key); keep the existing clauses.
